_help: Per commodity, an indicator->1-5 map (5 = bullish). A bare number or {"score": n, "note": "why"} for auditability. Unset = held at neutral and excluded from the average, exactly like fundamentals_manual. Refreshed by the fx-strength-desk-daily task, step 2c.

Real yield direction.note: Headwind worsened again: the 10-year broke above the mid-Sep 5.01-5.04% peak to ~5.17% on 25 Sep (hovering near 5.2%, highest since 2007) on hawkish Fedspeak (Barr, Williams, Hammack all pointing to another hike) and energy-driven inflation expectations. The 23 Sep 'no longer extending' read is superseded, so cut back from 2 to 1.5.

US dollar direction.note: DXY held above 101 on 25 Sep (101.03), after four straight up sessions - strongest in nearly two months and a second weekly gain, up ~1.9% on the month, on Oct FOMC hike odds (~60%+). Firming headwind, cut from 2 to 1.5.

Central-bank & ETF demand.note: Divergence continues: central banks bought a record 289 tonnes in Q2 2026 (PBoC extending an 18-month buying streak) even as Western gold ETFs saw net outflows of ~45 tonnes over the same window - but the outflow narrative flipped short-term into the 16 Sep FOMC, with GLD+GLDM taking in a combined ~$2bn over five trading days just ahead of the hike. Net still bullish on the CB leg with ETF flows choppy rather than a clean bleed, unchanged at 4.

Safe-haven bid.note: Hormuz talks stalled again over the weekend (Iran won't soften demands, Trump rejected its plan), which should help the haven leg - but gold slipped from ~$4,320 to ~$4,213 over the week as yields and the dollar dominated. Mixed, held at 3.

The 23 Sep 'no longer extending' read is superseded, so cut back from 2 to 1.5. Silver more leveraged to it than gold.

US dollar direction.note: DXY held above 101 on 25 Sep (101.03), after four straight up sessions - strongest in nearly two months and a second weekly gain, up ~1.9% on the month, on Oct FOMC hike odds (~60%+). Firming headwind, cut from 2 to 1.5.

Industrial demand.note: Re-checked: industrial leg is ebbing - JPMorgan sees solar silver demand down ~30% in 2026 and Metals Focus/Mercom put PV demand -19% y/y on thrifting and substitution (AGBI, 'solar demand loses shine', Sep 2026). A sixth straight deficit (~46 Moz) and record-low China inventories still support, but the old 'record demand' read is superseded; cut 3.5 -> 2.5.

Gold-silver ratio.note: Ratio ~67.9 (XAU 4213 / XAG 62.0 on the 28 Sep feed), up slightly from ~66.6 but still well below the long-run ~80 average. Neutral, unchanged.

OPEC+ supply policy.note: Re-checked: no new decision since 6 Sep, when the seven core members held October quotas at the September level (31.01 Mb/d) after completing the rollback of voluntary cuts; the group signalled quotas likely steady through year-end. Next meeting 4 Oct. Supply restraint intact, held at 4.

Inventory trend.note: EIA week to 18 Sep: crude +3.0 Mb to 426.4 Mb vs a ~0.6 Mb draw expected, now ~2% above the 5-year average (bearish), partly offset by gasoline -1.7 Mb (6% below 5-yr) and distillates -0.4 Mb (12% below). Crude build tilts it mildly bearish, 3 -> 2.5.

Demand outlook.note: Re-checked: the September IEA OMR is still the latest - 2026 demand to fall 2.5 mb/d (940 kb/d steeper than August) as the US-Iran impasse delays normal flows; EIA sees -1.7 mb/d, only OPEC sees growth. Held at 1.5.

Geopolitical risk premium.note: Talks stalled again: Trump rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz reopening proposal (blockade lifted, assets unfrozen, war ended 'on all fronts') and Iran said on 27 Sep it won't soften its demands - Brent back above $106, WTI ~$94 (Bloomberg). Strait still shut, so the 23 Sep de-escalation cut is partly reversed, 2 -> 3.
